lesson_scope: Vertical motion of single and multiple bodies under uniform gravity; selection and algebraic application of constant-acceleration equations with explicit sign conventions; determination of maximum height, apex velocity vanishing, time of flight, and duration spent at or above specified elevation thresholds; ascending carrier release problems and relative vertical trajectory crossings.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Initial speed and time to reach greatest height

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Initial speed and time to reach greatest height

hints: At the greatest height, the vertical velocity is instantaneously zero: $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$ to find $u^2 = 2(10)(45) = 900 \implies u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Then use $v = u - gt$ to get $t = \frac{30}{10} = 3\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with upward displacement $s = 45\text{ m}$, final velocity $v = 0$, and $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$0 = u^2 - 2(10)(45) = u^2 - 900$$
$$u = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the time taken to reach greatest height using $v = u + at$:
$$0 = 30 - 10t \implies 10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find initial velocity from peak altitude:
- At the apex, all kinetic energy is converted into gravitational potential:
$$u = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(10)(45)} = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine ascent time:
- Gravity slows the particle by $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ every second:
$$t = \frac{30}{10} = 3\text{ s}$$
The particle leaves the ground at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and takes $3\text{ s}$ to reach its peak.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$ with $v = 0$ and $s = 45$ to find $u$, or applies $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ from apex to find $t$.
Obtains initial speed $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and time to greatest height $t = 3\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Duration spent at or above a given height threshold

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Duration spent at or above a given height threshold

hints: Set the displacement formula $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ equal to $40\text{ m}$ with $u = 30$ and $g = 10$.
Rearrange $30t - 5t^2 = 40$ to $t^2 - 6t + 8 = 0$. The roots are $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$, so the duration spent above $40\text{ m}$ is $4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the height equation with $s = 40\text{ m}$, $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \implies 40 = 30t - 5t^2$$
$$5t^2 - 30t + 40 = 0 \implies t^2 - 6t + 8 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation for the two passage times:
$$(t - 2)(t - 4) = 0 \implies t_1 = 2\text{ s}, \quad t_2 = 4\text{ s}$$
$$\Delta t = t_2 - t_1 = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the times of crossing $40\text{ m}$:
- Setting vertical position to $40\text{ m}$:
$$5t^2 - 30t + 40 = 0 \implies t^2 - 6t + 8 = 0$$
- Factoring gives upward and downward times:
$$(t - 2)(t - 4) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}, \; 4\text{ s}$$

Compute time spent above the boundary:
- Subtract the upward crossing from the downward crossing:
$$\Delta t = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$$
The particle remains at or above $40\text{ m}$ for exactly $2\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up displacement equation $30t - 5t^2 = 40$ and forms quadratic $t^2 - 6t + 8 = 0$.
Solves for crossing times $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$ to obtain duration $\Delta t = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Determining height threshold from time interval above it

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Determining height threshold from time interval above it

hints: The motion above height $h$ is symmetrical about the apex. Time to apex is $t_{\text{apex}} = \frac{35}{10} = 3.5\text{ s}$.

Since the particle spends $3\text{ s}$ above $h$, it takes $\frac{3}{2} = 1.5\text{ s}$ from height $h$ to the apex. Thus it crosses $h$ upwards at $t_1 = 3.5 - 1.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$. Evaluate $h = 35(2) - 5(4) = 50\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the time to reach maximum height:
$$t_{\text{apex}} = \frac{u}{g} = \frac{35}{10} = 3.5\text{ s}$$
By symmetry, the $3\text{ s}$ duration above $h$ is split equally before and after the apex:
$$t_{\text{ascent above } h} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\text{ s} \implies t_1 = 3.5 - 1.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$$

Calculate the height $h$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$h = ut_1 - \frac{1}{2}gt_1^2 = 35(2) - 5(2^2) = 70 - 20 = 50\text{ m}$$
Alternatively, from maximum height $H_{\max} = \frac{35^2}{20} = 61.25\text{ m}$:
$$h = H_{\max} - \frac{1}{2}g(1.5^2) = 61.25 - 5(2.25) = 61.25 - 11.25 = 50\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Exploit symmetry about the peak:
- Apex occurs at $t = 3.5\text{ s}$:
$$t_{\text{apex}} = \frac{35}{10} = 3.5\text{ s}$$
- Spending $3\text{ s}$ above level $h$ means climbing for $1.5\text{ s}$ to peak:
$$t_1 = 3.5 - 1.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$$

Compute elevation $h$:
- Evaluating position at $t = 2.0\text{ s}$:
$$h = 35(2) - 5(4) = 70 - 20 = 50\text{ m}$$
The threshold height is exactly $50\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds time to greatest height $t_{\text{apex}} = 3.5\text{ s}$ and deduces upward crossing occurs at $t_1 = 3.5 - 1.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$.
Evaluates $h = 35(2) - 5(2^2)$ to obtain $h = 50\text{ m}$.

hints: Substitute $s = 19\text{ m}$, $u = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.

walkthrough.text:

$$(t - 1)(5t - 19) = 0$$
$$t_1 = 1\text{ s}, \quad t_2 = \frac{19}{5} = 3.8\text{ s}$$
$$\Delta t = t_2 - t_1 = 3.8 - 1.0 = 2.8\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:

$$(t - 1)(5t - 19) = 0 \implies t = 1.0\text{ s}, \; 3.8\text{ s}$$
- Duration spent above $19\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta t = 3.8 - 1.0 = 2.8\text{ s}$$
The particle remains higher than $19\text{ m}$ for $2.8\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Projectile launched from an elevated balcony

hints: Displacement from the balcony to the ground is $s = -15\text{ m}$ when taking upwards as positive.
Apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$: $v^2 = 10^2 + 2(-10)(-15) = 100 + 300 = 400$, giving impact speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Then use $v = u + at$ with $v = -20$ to find $T = 3\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the speed just before impact with displacement $s = -15\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 10^2 + 2(-10)(-15)$$
$$v^2 = 100 + 300 = 400 \implies |v| = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the total flight time $T$ using $v = u + at$ with downward velocity $v = -20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$-20 = 10 - 10T \implies 10T = 30 \implies T = 3\text{ s}$$
Alternatively, solve the position quadratic directly:
$$-15 = 10T - 5T^2 \implies 5T^2 - 10T - 15 = 0 \implies T^2 - 2T - 3 = 0$$
$$(T - 3)(T + 1) = 0 \implies T = 3\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine striking speed:
- Net displacement to ground is $-15\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 10^2 + 2(-10)(-15) = 400$$
- The speed magnitude is:
$$v = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate overall journey duration:
- Velocity changes from $+10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $-20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ under $-10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ acceleration:
$$T = \frac{-20 - 10}{-10} = \frac{-30}{-10} = 3\text{ s}$$
The ball hits the ground at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ after $3\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 3: Two particles projected vertically upwards at different times

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Two particles projected vertically upwards at different times

hints: Let $t$ be the time elapsed from the launch of particle $A$. Since particle $B$ is launched $1\text{ s}$ later, its travel time is $(t - 1)$ for $t \ge 1$.
Write the height formula for each particle: $h_A = 30t - 5t^2$ and $h_B = 35(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equate $h_A = h_B$: the quadratic terms $-5t^2$ cancel on both sides, leaving $30t = 45t - 40 \implies 15t = 40 \implies t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s} \approx 2.67\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the vertical displacements of particles $A$ and $B$ in terms of time $t$ from the launch of $A$:
$$h_A = 30t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 30t - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = 35(t - 1) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2 = 35(t - 1) - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1)$$
$$h_B = 35t - 35 - 5t^2 + 10t - 5 = 45t - 5t^2 - 40$$

Equate the heights $h_A = h_B$ and solve for $t$:
$$30t - 5t^2 = 45t - 5t^2 - 40$$
$$30t = 45t - 40 \implies 15t = 40$$
$$t = \frac{40}{15} = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s} \approx 2.67\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate altitude equations:
- Particle $A$ has been in flight for $t$ seconds:
$$h_A = 30t - 5t^2$$
- Particle $B$ started $1\text{ s}$ later, so its time is $(t - 1)$:
$$h_B = 35(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2 = 45t - 5t^2 - 40$$

Equate altitudes:
- Notice the gravity terms $-5t^2$ balance and cancel completely:
$$30t = 45t - 40 \implies 15t = 40$$
- Solving gives:
$$t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s} \approx 2.67\text{ s}$$
The particles reach the same height $2.67\text{ s}$ after particle $A$ is fired.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses height of $A$ as $h_A = 30t - 5t^2$ and height of $B$ as $h_B = 35(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equates $h_A = h_B$ to form linear equation $30t - 5t^2 = 45t - 5t^2 - 40$.
Solves for time to obtain $t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s} \approx 2.67\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Two particles projected vertically upwards at different times

hints: Substitute $t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s}$ into $h_A = 30t - 5t^2$ to calculate the height.
Evaluate: $30\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) - 5\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^2 = 80 - 5\left(\frac{64}{9}\right) = 80 - \frac{320}{9} = \frac{400}{9} \approx 44.4\text{ m}$.
To determine whether $A$ is rising or falling, evaluate its velocity $v_A = u - gt$ at $t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s}$.
Since $v_A = 30 - 10\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = 30 - \frac{80}{3} = +\frac{10}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1} > 0$, particle $A$ is still travelling upwards (rising).

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the meeting height by substituting $t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s}$ into the height expression for $A$:
$$h = 30\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) - 5\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^2 = 80 - 5\left(\frac{64}{9}\right)$$
$$h = 80 - \frac{320}{9} = \frac{720 - 320}{9} = \frac{400}{9}\text{ m} \approx 44.4\text{ m}$$

Determine the direction of motion of particle $A$ from its velocity:
$$v_A = u_A - gt = 30 - 10\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = 30 - \frac{80}{3} = +\frac{10}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx +3.33\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Since } v_A > 0, \text{ particle } A \text{ is still rising}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate meeting altitude:
- Evaluating position of $A$ at $t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ s}$:
$$h = 30\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) - 5\left(\frac{64}{9}\right) = 80 - 35.56 = 44.44\text{ m}$$
- In exact fractional form:
$$h = \frac{400}{9}\text{ m} \approx 44.4\text{ m}$$

Check instantaneous velocity of $A$:
- Particle $A$ has apex at $t = 3\text{ s}$. Since $2.67\text{ s} < 3.0\text{ s}$:
$$v_A = 30 - 10(2.67) = +3.33\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Because velocity is positive, particle $A$ is on its upward climb.

hints: Taking upwards as positive from the release point, ground level corresponds to $s = -60\text{ m}$.
Take the square root: impact speed is $v = \sqrt{1225} = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find flight time from $v = u + at$ with downward velocity $v = -35$: $-35 = 5 - 10T \implies 10T = 40 \implies T = 4\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the total time of flight $T$ using $v = u + at$ with downward velocity $v = -35\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$-35 = 5 - 10T \implies 10T = 40 \implies T = 4\text{ s}$$
Alternatively, solve the position quadratic:
$$-60 = 5T - 5T^2 \implies 5T^2 - 5T - 60 = 0 \implies T^2 - T - 12 = 0$$
$$(T - 4)(T + 3) = 0 \implies T = 4\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute terminal impact velocity:
- Net drop to ground is $-60\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 5^2 + 2(-10)(-60) = 1225$$
- The speed of collision is:
$$v = \sqrt{1225} = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate flight time:

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone 1: Dropped and projected stones crossing in flight between cliff and ground

hints: Write expressions for the height above the ground of both stones at time $t$.
For stone $A$ dropped from $120\text{ m}$: $h_A = 120 - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 120 - 5t^2$. For stone $B$ launched from ground: $h_B = Ut - 5t^2$.
Equate $h_A = h_B$: $120 - 5t^2 = Ut - 5t^2 \implies Ut = 120$, which establishes $t = \frac{120}{U}$.
The stones meet at height $75\text{ m}$, so set $h_A = 75$: $120 - 5t^2 = 75 \implies 5t^2 = 45 \implies t^2 = 9 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$.
Substitute $t = 3\text{ s}$ into $Ut = 120$: $3U = 120 \implies U = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write expressions for the elevation above ground level of both stones at time $t$:
$$h_A = 120 - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 120 - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = Ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = Ut - 5t^2$$
Equate the heights to find the time of passing:
$$120 - 5t^2 = Ut - 5t^2 \implies Ut = 120 \implies t = \frac{120}{U}$$

Use the given meeting elevation ($75\text{ m}$) to determine $t$ and $U$:
$$h_A = 120 - 5t^2 = 75$$
$$5t^2 = 45 \implies t^2 = 9 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
Substitute $t = 3\text{ s}$ into $t = \frac{120}{U}$:
$$3 = \frac{120}{U} \implies U = \frac{120}{3} = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare heights above ground:
- Stone $A$ descends from the cliff top:
$$h_A = 120 - 5t^2$$
- Stone $B$ ascends from ground level:
$$h_B = Ut - 5t^2$$
- Equating positions cancels gravity:
$$120 = Ut \implies t = \frac{120}{U}$$

Determine the projection speed $U$:
- Since meeting occurs at $75\text{ m}$ altitude:
$$120 - 5t^2 = 75 \implies 5t^2 = 45 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
- Substituting $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$U = \frac{120}{3} = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Stone $B$ is projected with speed $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Meeting occurs at $t = 3\text{ s}$. Evaluate the velocity of both stones at this instant.

Stone $B$ was projected upwards at $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $v_B = U - gt = 40 - 10(3) = +10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed upwards.
Since $v_B = +10\text{ m s}^{-1} > 0$, stone $B$ is still ascending as it passes stone $A$.

Calculate the velocity of stone $A$ at the meeting time $t = 3\text{ s}$:

$$v^2 = U^2 - 2gH_{\max, B} \implies 0 = 40^2 - 2(10)H_{\max, B}$$

$$H_{\max} = \frac{40^2}{20} = 80\text{ m}$$

Consider the upward stage from point $B$ to the highest point $C$ ($t_{BC} = 2\text{ s}$, $v_C = 0$):
$$v_C = v_B - gt_{BC} \implies 0 = v_B - 10(2)$$
$$v_B = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Consider the interval from point $A$ to point $B$ ($t_{AB} = 1\text{ s}$):
$$v_B = v_A - gt_{AB} \implies 20 = v_A - 10(1)$$
$$v_A = 20 + 10 = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

$$s_{AB} = \left(\frac{v_A + v_B}{2}\right)t_{AB} = \left(\frac{30 + 20}{2}\right)(1) = 25\text{ m}$$

hints: The particle takes $1\text{ s}$ from launch $O$ to reach point $A$ where $v_A = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

$$h_A = ut_{OA} - \frac{1}{2}gt_{OA}^2 = 40(1) - 5(1^2) = 35\text{ m}$$

$$v_A^2 = u^2 - 2gh_A \implies 30^2 = 40^2 - 20h_A \implies 20h_A = 1600 - 900 = 700 \implies h_A = 35\text{ m}$$

$$h_B = h_A + 25 = 35 + 25 = 60\text{ m}$$
$$h_C = \frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{40^2}{2(10)} = \frac{1600}{20} = 80\text{ m}$$

$$h_C = h_B + \frac{v_B^2}{2g} = 60 + \frac{20^2}{20} = 60 + 20 = 80\text{ m}$$

Determine launch velocity:
- At $t = 1\text{ s}$, speed has dropped from $u$ to $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$u = 30 + 10(1) = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

$$h_A = 40(1) - 5(1) = 35\text{ m}$$

Compute higher milestones $h_B$ and $h_C$:
- Checkpoint $B$ is $25\text{ m}$ higher:
$$h_B = 35 + 25 = 60\text{ m}$$
- Maximum height $h_C$ at apex:
$$h_C = \frac{40^2}{20} = 80\text{ m}$$
